$ xref profile report

by Alexander Panasenko · xrefcode.com
On this page

Summarize a recorded profile (.xprof, from live profile or profile import): the hottest functions, basic blocks, source lines, caller paths or instructions, with self and total shares.

Usage

xref profile report [OPTIONS] <PROFILE>

Arguments and options

Arguments

<PROFILE>
The .xprof recording.

Options

--top <TOP>
Number of rows to print.
default 30
--by <BY>
What a row aggregates: function, basic block, source line, caller path, instruction, or thread (each thread with its hottest functions). Values: function; block; line; caller-path; instruction; thread (Each thread with its samples and the functions they were in).
default function
--json
Print the report as JSON.
--folded <FOLDED>
Also write folded stacks (flame-graph input) to this file.
--within <WITHIN>
Keep samples whose call chain includes this function or address.
--window <WINDOW>
Select one captured trigger window (numbered from one).
--merge-windows
Report the union of all captured windows.
--from <FROM>
Keep the samples from this time on, in seconds from the first sample (12, 2.5 or 500ms).
--to <TO>
Keep the samples before this time, in seconds from the first sample.

Examples

The profile is ripgrep filtering an endless input stream, recorded with live profile.

A time window

A profile of a whole run mixes start-up, the steady state and teardown. --from and --to keep the samples of one span, in seconds counted from the first sample of the recording; every view (--by, --within, --folded, --json) reads only those samples:

Command
# Skip the first 5 seconds of loading and stop before teardown:
xref -b ./app profile report app.xprof --from 5 --to 25

The report says what it kept, after the first line:

time window: 5.000 s to 25.000 s of 31.212 s from the first sample; 4987 samples before it and 6201 after left out, 0 lost in it

The lost count of the first line is that of the whole recording.

A recording whose samples carry no timestamps (perf script text written without the time field) is refused, and so is a span with no samples in it. A recording made with a trigger keeps its own windows, selected with --window.

Reading the output

  • The first line: samples, lost and dropped samples, and partial=true when some call chains could not be unwound completely.
  • Each row: self share (samples in the function itself), total share (samples with the function anywhere on the stack), self sample count, and the frame: target:fn_ADDR for code in the binary, target:unknown for samples in the binary outside any known function, [kernel] or a library for the rest.
  • Library frames are named like the binary's (libc.so.6:memset), from the library's own .symtab and .dynsym. A stripped library is also named from its separate debug file (/usr/lib/debug/.build-id/…, .gnu_debuglink, or debuginfod when DEBUGINFOD_URLS is set and debuginfod-find is installed), which has the internal names such as __memset_avx2_unaligned_erms. Without one, an internal implementation that an exported IFUNC resolver selects is named after the IFUNC (memset). Kernel frames are named from /proc/kallsyms (readable as root), except code of loadable modules, whose addresses can be reused within a boot, and [vdso] frames from the vdso. Both get names only when the report runs in the boot the recording was made in, because kernel addresses change with every boot.
  • warning: lines name the reasons a chain stopped; they are counted, not hidden.
  • note: lines say when the report is likely to mislead, and what to do:
    • With frame-pointer callchains (perf record -g, live profile --callers fp), when 10% or more of the samples are in library functions. A library built without frame pointers (glibc's memcmp, memcpy) hides or misnames the direct caller of those functions, so check their callers with a --call-graph dwarf recording.
    • For a profile import with a base taken from --base, --maps or perf script text, when fewer than half of the return addresses in the target's call chains follow a call instruction (with 50 or more checked). With a correct base every one does. A base that is off by even one page still names functions, just the wrong ones. The report is then marked partial.

Provenance

Recorded with xref 0.7.0 (the remapped release build of commit db9b69e, made by scripts/package-release.sh before the tag) on Linux x86-64, on rg = ripgrep 14.1.1 (official stripped release). Output is unchanged except that whitespace at the end of each line and empty lines at the end of the output are removed; long outputs are cut where marked.
